chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abdul Kareem, from Al-Hasan Al-Sayqal, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who divorces his wife with a divorce that makes her not permissible to him until she marries another husband, and a man marries her with a temporary marriage, would she be permissible for him if he marries her? He (peace be upon him) said: No, until she enters into what she has come out from.

key_terms.مِثْلِ مَا خَرَجَتْ مِنْهُ: what she has come out from (referring to the type of marriage)

ai.seo_question: Does a temporary marriage count as a valid second marriage for a triple-divorced woman to become permissible to her first husband?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the fiqh of 'Taliqah' by rejecting the validity of temporary marriage (Mut'ah) as a sufficient bridge for remarriage to the first husband, a key point of contention between Shia and Sunni jurisprudence. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) specifies that the second marriage must be a full, permanent union that is consummated, ensuring the woman truly 'exits' the state of being bound to her first husband before returning. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on the permanence and consummation of the intermediate marriage to prevent the practice of 'Taliqah' from becoming a mere formality.
